transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-03-11 15:00 UTC | Duration 54m | Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Samira (Redwood SE), Dr. Maria Gomez, Ethan Park, Priya Nair

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jordan Patel, AE at Redwood. Uh, quick check, can everyone see the agenda I dropped in the chat? Link: https://redwood.ai/docs/eval-plan (note: link is placeholder)
[00:12] Maria: Yep got it, thanks Jordan. Appreciate you making time.
[00:18] Jordan: Great. Samira from our SE team will co-run; we want to nail the POC success criteria, workload sizing, and then walk through the proposed quality evaluation plan 
dgolden prompts, regression tests, hallucination checks, scoring.
[00:30] Samira: Hi all. Quick intro: I'll be doing the benchmark runs and helping design the eval harness. We'll propose both automated metrics and a lightweight manual review protocol.
[00:40] Priya: Quick context 
dour priority is a clinical notes summarization assistant for primary care docs. Success is both accuracy of extracted problems/meds and the format compliance for EHR ingestion. Timeline: 6 week POC ideally.
[00:54] Jordan: Nice. Ok, step one 
d success criteria. What would you consider an automatic pass versus needs-work?
[01:05] Maria: For us, automatic pass would be >=92% entity extraction precision on the golden set, recall above 90, and hallucination rate under 3% measured per 100 outputs. Latency target: single-response p50 < 450ms, p95 < 900ms. Cost goal: under $0.30 per 1k tokens equivalent on average.
[01:30] Ethan: Also format adherence 
output must match our JSON schema 99% of the time or we need fallback. If formatting breaks, our ingestion pipeline chokes.
[01:44] Samira: Good concrete numbers. We'll map those to the eval plan. Note 
sometimes token counting differs between toolings, we'll normalize to Redwood's token metric.
[01:55] Jordan: Great. Now the workload sizing 
how many requests/day and typical prompt sizes?
[02:02] Priya: Baseline is 30k requests/day, average prompt 220 tokens, peak 200 RPS in a burst window. For POC we'll scale down to a 10k request/day bench.
[02:20] Jordan: So POC bench target: 10k/day with 200 RPS simulated bursts. Good. That informs batching and concurrency on our side.
[02:30] Maria: One more 
some prompts are longer, up to 1,200 tokens when including patient history, so we need to test tail latency and KV cache behavior for long context.
[02:45] Samira: Noted 
we'll include a long-context subset in the golden prompts.
[02:52] Jordan: Ok, moving to quality eval plan. I'll read our high-level approach, Samira will fill in metrics and tests.
[03:00] Samira: Plan overview: 1) Golden prompt suite 
~350 prompts representative across clinics (short, medium, long). 2) Ground-truth labels for entities & structured fields (CSV + JSON). 3) Automated metrics: precision/recall/F1 for entities, format-parse rate, hallucination detection via rule-based checks & sampling. 4) Regression tests vs baseline model (we'll compare against your existing model and an open checkpoint). 5) Human-in-the-loop spot checks 
200 manual reviews for edge cases.
[03:33] Maria: On hallucination detection 
can you elaborate on method? We can't just rely on keyword matches.
[03:41] Samira: Yeah, good point. We propose two-tier: automatic heuristics for obvious contradictions (e.g., output cites a lab result value not present in prompt), plus a fact-check microservice where we attempt to align extracted entities against the ground-truth source fields. Then sample-based human review to measure false negatives. We report hallucination rate as percent of outputs with at least one hallucinated fact.
[04:05] Ethan: How do you handle format enforcement? If model spits free text, can we force JSON output?
[04:12] Samira: We'll use both constrained decoding + post-parse validators. Constrained decoding to bias generation towards the schema, plus a strict parser that flags and auto-attempts fixes. For POC we'll measure format-parse success and also measure the success after 1 attempt of automatic repair.
[04:30] Jordan: Scoring approach 
we'll produce a composite score composed of weighted metrics: entity-F1 (40%), hallucination penalty (20%), format-parse rate (20%), latency/cost SLO adherence (20%). Each submetric normalized to 0-100 then weighted; pass threshold 80 composite.
[04:53] Priya: Can you show an example scoring calc?
[04:57] Samira: Sure. Example: entity-F1 88 => normalized 88; hallucination 2% => we map to a 95; format-parse 98% => 98; latency/cost SLO meets 1 of 2 => 85. Weighted composite = 0.4*88 + 0.2*95 + 0.2*98 + 0.2*85 = 35.2 + 19 + 19.6 + 17 = 90.8 => pass. We'll include the exact mapping functions in the plan doc.
[05:30] Jordan: Nice. Regression tests 
we'll baseline against two models: your current in-house baseline and Redwood's curated open checkpoint (we can specify model names in the doc). Want us to run both?
[05:42] Maria: Yes please, baseline + Redwood recommended. Also include temperature sweeps and quantized variants so we can evaluate cost/perf tradeoffs.
[05:54] Samira: We'll run: (A) hosted default (our recommended), (B) small quantized variant, (C) your baseline (if you provide model or outputs). For each we measure the full metric suite.
[06:06] Ethan: For the hallucination samples, we want a reproducible set of prompts to test. Will you keep random seeds?
[06:12] Samira: Absolutely 
everything is deterministic in the harness with fixed seeds; we'll commit the run config to the repo we share.
[06:20] Jordan: Security and data controls 
reminder we support VPC/private deployment options but for the POC hosted is fine if we get a limited, anonymized dataset. We'll need an NDA signed and the SOC2 package link.
[06:35] Maria: NDA is done. We'll share anonymized data to an S3 bucket with temporary creds. Also need to review your data retention and KMS encryption notes.
[06:44] Jordan: We'll send the security doc link and SOC2 artifact. Link to security pack: https://redwood.ai/security (placeholder).
[06:51] Priya: Back to timeline 
you mentioned 6 weeks; can you break out phases?
[06:58] Samira: Phase 0 (prep, week 0): dataset share + golden prompt list. Phase 1 (week 1-2): initial benchmark runs and latency/cost baseline. Phase 2 (week 3-4): iterative tuning (prompt engineering, constrained decoding, quantization trials). Phase 3 (week 5): final regression runs + manual review. Week 6: final report + go/no-go. We'll align exact calendar dates once we get the dataset share.
[07:25] Maria: Sounds good. Any blocking items from Redwood?
[07:29] Jordan: We'll need a point person to provide ground-truth labels and a small team to review manual checks 
at least 3 clinical SMEs for the 200 manual reviews.
[07:40] Ethan: We can provide two SMEs and recruit one more from an external reviewer pool 
fine.
[07:47] Priya: How will you surface hallucination examples? Prefer a spreadsheet with snippets and tags so we can triage.
[07:54] Samira: We'll publish a Google Sheet with sample outputs, classification (hallucination type, severity), and original prompt. Also link to the run artifacts and the evaluation script in a GitHub repo we share.
[08:08] Jordan: Any concerns about rate limits or concurrency during bench? We can provision Dedicated slack if you need guaranteed throughput.
[08:16] Maria: For POC probably hosted is fine, but if we see p95 latency issues we may ask for a short Dedicated window.
[08:24] Samira: Noted. We'll monitor and flag capacity fallbacks; Redwood has automatic fallback policies but we'll avoid noisy degradations.
[08:33] Jordan: Ok, doc artifacts we will share: 1) Detailed eval plan PDF, 2) Golden prompt CSV + sample script, 3) Run config + seed, 4) Benchmark spreadsheet template, 5) Security pack.
[08:47] Priya: Can you also include a short section on prompt variants you plan to test (zero-shot, few-shot with 3 examples, and system message tweaks)?
[08:56] Samira: Yes 
we will include these variants in the golden suite and report per-variant metrics.
[09:03] Maria: For scoring, how do you handle borderline clinical errors? Not all hallucinations are equal.
[09:09] Samira: We'll annotate severity levels: critical (could cause clinical harm), major (incorrect but non-harmful), minor (format/typo). Our composite score will weight critical errors heavily and we provide separate pass/fail gates for critical error thresholds (e.g., zero tolerance or <0.1% depending on risk appetite).
[09:32] Ethan: Are you able to run an initial smoke test on a small holdout today?
[09:37] Samira: We can do a very small quick check if you drop a tiny sample into the S3 link now, but full runs require the harness and the label mapping.
[09:46] Maria: I'll upload a 50-record sample right after this call. Expect an email with the S3 path.
[09:52] Jordan: Perfect. We'll aim to return a quick smoke report within 48 hours of sample arrival.
[09:59] Priya: Anything about compliance 
need to ensure logs are scrubbed during POC.
[10:03] Jordan: Logs can be restricted and scrubbed; we'll follow your retention policy for POC and encrypt at rest.
[10:10] Samira: Small note 
where you said KV cash earlier in a demo, I think you meant KV cache 
just call out that long contexts use the KV cache; some transcriptions confuse it.
[10:20] (laughter) Maria: Yeah that was me 
I say cash sometimes.
[10:24] Jordan: OK, final recap of next steps: Jordan sends the draft eval plan and golden prompts; Maria uploads sample dataset; Samira runs baseline and shares sheet; schedule full benchmark week of 2025-03-24.
[10:40] Priya: That timeline works for us. Thanks all.
[10:45] Jordan: Thanks team, we'll follow up in email with links and the plan.
[10:50] Maria: Appreciate it, bye.
[10:52] End of call.
